### Cancellation on the shared private control transport and scheduler

The existing private index-control request now admits cleanup, completion and
cancel-release operations. They use the same HTTP route, in-process receiving
port, service-authority/deadline gates and post-commit signing machinery as
ordinary index controls. There is no separate cancellation route or public
relational-index API. Providers without the complete cancellation contract fail
closed rather than exposing only part of that lifecycle.

Replies carry compact scoped progress and, when available, the complete signed
ACK. They do not duplicate schema/manifest/cleanup outcome bodies. Progress alone,
physical GC completion, pending replication or failed signing cannot acknowledge
an owner. Validation binds request identity, native cut, action, root generation
and witness/signature; local delivery retains ownership until serialization or
consumption finishes.

The bounded worker resumes canceling/cancel-releasing jobs. Each turn executes
one receiving-port or metadata operation: cleanup advances at most one admitted
native effect/page, completion obtains a signed durable cleanup checkpoint, and
release uses metadata's all-owner barrier. ACK proposals and lost-reply status
resolution reuse the existing ACK state machine. The all-owner barrier still
prevents one owner's early local retirement from lifting the cohort's fences.

Residency now reserves cohort capture and completed-owner recovery work in
addition to the fixed useful-work allowance. A 4,096-owner capture/sweep cannot
consume the entire allowance and repeatedly restart at the same completed prefix.
The source-EOF recovery reservation derives from the producer state machine, not
only the cheaper acknowledged-control path. Jobs/actors, per-turn effects and
page memory stay bounded. This is work-count/liveness accounting, not a measured
latency or large-cluster throughput claim; a pending-owner directory remains a
possible improvement over repeated cohort sweeps.

### Exact online-index admission observation

### SQL regular UNIQUE admission and request-shaped completion

Regular SQL `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` now lowers to the owned private publication

required reader/runtime or publication capabilities reject before admission;
there is no unsafe schema-first fallback or native alias for Raft execution.

Lost internal begin replies, OOM while constructing acknowledgements, malformed responses and
unmirrored observations reconcile only the exact immutable admission identity.

headroom rejection is a retryable catalog-publication precondition, not a generic
internal error or an ambiguous admitted write. The prepared schema/catalog/cohort

keeps regular write-fenced builds distinct from CONCURRENTLY; concurrent syntax

### Request-shaped durable index cancellation

Pgwire cancellation and statement deadlines now enter a bounded, separately
budgeted recovery lane for the exact admitted index job. The lane preserves
request authority, clears only the expired client cancellation/deadline, and
uses a two-second cleanup budget. HTTP bounded observation never cancels an
asynchronous build. Transport/executor failures without a client cancellation
or expired statement deadline do not manufacture cancellation intent.

Each cancel CAS binds table/job/revision plus the observed metadata incarnation
and immutable plan digest. Metadata checks that guard in the same transaction
as cancellation, including apply/replay, not only in a preceding read. Protocol
floor 54 adds an explicit guard-presence encoding; older private cancellation
bytes are rejected and all index-publication stages use the coordinated floor.
Current owner-failure workers retain their current-authority cancellation form.

After a lost cancel reply, the lane observes only the exact job. It never repeats
the same revision-CAS. A strictly newer committed pre-publication head can admit
a new CAS because the old expected revision can no longer match. Cancellation
admission is not rollback: definitive cancellation is returned only after the
terminal canceled head proves cleanup and fence release. Irreversible publication,
unmirrored/foreign observations, or exhausted cleanup budget preserve a pending
receipt and token rather than claiming abort. Unknown admission remains unknown
unless an exact confirmed observation establishes the job.

This connects request cancellation to the durable job, not complete real-owner
wire/distributed cancellation qualification. Hosted/Raft execution, replacement
root adoption and client-preowned recovery for an entirely lost public response
remain open. Original SQL dispositions are unchanged.

### Native physical-root process ownership

Native standalone now retains an exclusive `std.Io` file lease on the replica
root before admitting its physical native binding. This closes the gap in the
catalog-path operator lock: independent catalog directories pointing at the same
replica root previously had independent catalog locks. The root lease lives
until DataServer and metadata work have shut down. Its stable inode is never
truncated or unlinked by production code. Opening uses nonblocking exclusive
locking and rejects a symlinked sentinel; subsequent checks detect a missing or
replaced sentinel. Durable root UUID and signing checks remain separate.

receiver's shared owner-decision read also requires and checks it before any
storage effect. That filesystem validation runs outside the metadata mutex.
Metadata-only observations do not invent a physical receiver or acquire a lease.

node/store mismatches and unsupported hosted/Raft compositions fail closed.

### Original join cohort: schema-bound USING/NATURAL and native bag semantics

The 22-original `sql_join_read_campaign.json` executes unchanged source SQL
through mounted HTTP handlers over two immutable typed local tables. A fresh
PostgreSQL 18+ process independently verifies column names/OIDs, values, SQL
NULL flags and complete ordered peer frontiers. Distinct physical keys preserve
duplicate logical rows; the witness includes missing customers, NULL keys,
missing amounts, nullable Boolean cells and cross-table unmatched customers.
OFFSET cuts are independently checked not to split a peer group. Golden output
generation fails closed rather than overwriting a reference with exclusions.

This campaign found actual parser gaps in `JOIN ... USING` and `NATURAL JOIN`.
The AST now preserves declarative keys until catalog binding. Binding produces
ordinary equality predicates through shared composite hash-key extraction,
plus typed merged-key projections. Unqualified keys and plain stars expose one
merged cell; qualified names/stars retain each original input key and order.
INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL, composite keys, chained joins and USING aliases share
this machinery. NATURAL discovers only visible keys on both inputs, never an
implicit physical row ID. An explicitly named hidden ID remains addressable.
Missing, duplicate and ambiguous keys, and colliding USING aliases, fail before
capture; alias collisions use PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 42712.

Merged projections participate in cold-column dependency propagation. At the
statement boundary, a validated pure merged projection is eliminated if no new
identity is consumed (for example COUNT(*) or qualified-only projections).
This occurs after binding and does not change nested join ordinal layouts or
skip validation. A 256-by-256 duplicate-key work-limit test proves composite
hash extraction remains enabled and allocation counts stay below 4096 and
within twice the equivalent ON-join count plus 512. This is an allocation-work
regression, not a throughput/latency benchmark claim. Exhaustive allocator-fault
coverage checks coordinated-capture release, alongside existing outer-join,
CTE, snapshot and residual-predicate regressions in Debug.

### Typed streaming array expansion

The next large document-read cohort depends on array expansion. FROM UNNEST
now has an explicit schema-independent AST and a typed relational operator,
instead of treating a row producer as a scalar call or expanding JSON documents.
Binding shares existing parameter, lexical-scope, shape, decision-capability,
cold-projection and coordinated-capture boundaries. It retains scalar element
identities, including integer widths, UUID, exact NUMERIC and JSONB. EXPLAIN
exposes an Unnest node. Recursive dependency and subquery-scope visitors see
function inputs rather than hiding their references.

Execution evaluates each invocation's input arrays once and streams flat
storage-order elements. Multi-array calls zip to the longest input with SQL
NULL padding; empty and NULL arrays emit no rows by themselves. WITH ORDINALITY
starts at one regardless of array lower bounds. Implicit/explicit lateral
inputs and LEFT null extension use the existing Apply owner and captured cut.
Only emitted cells cross the output ownership boundary, not whole duplicated
arrays per expanded row. Expanded rows are charged to a statement-wide quota,
with cancellation checkpoints and allocator-failure cleanup.

Direct invariant UNNEST operators bypass eager expanded-row replay: LIMIT 1
over a prepared 10,001-element array succeeds with a one-row expansion quota,
both alone and beside a captured table. Scalar input preparation/work limits
remain independent and unchanged. Generic invariant derived-query replay and
other set-returning functions remain separate architectural work; this
checkpoint does not claim every enclosing plan is prefix-lazy.

An owned PostgreSQL 18+ server independently verifies 17 shared operator
contracts, including stored arrays, multi-dimensional/lower-bound order, exact
NUMERIC, UUID, JSON null versus SQL NULL and lateral outer joins. The native
executor consumes that same reference at page sizes 1, 3 and 64, checking exact
element OIDs, values and NULL flags. Mounted HTTP tests use actual typed storage
and bounded native captures. These references preserve bigint/NUMERIC wire
strings exactly; they never round them through a floating-point matcher. The
oracle uses a read-only server-side cursor and bounded fetches. PostgreSQL also
establishes that only the unqualified multi-array spelling is grammar sugar;
schema-qualified UNNEST retains its single-array signature.

### Replay ownership and prefix demand across expansion boundaries

A new negative workload reproduced a real gap: wrapping UNNEST in a lateral
derived SELECT caused invariant expanded rows to be eagerly materialized before
LIMIT 1. The 10,001-element prepared-array case failed its one-row expansion
quota in `/private/tmp/antfly-sql-unnest-derived-baseline.log`.

Bound relational nodes now carry a conservative replay policy: captured,
restartable, or streaming. This is an ownership/effect property, not an estimated
row count or a claim that every operator can stream. Binding computes it once
from child owners and bound expression volatility, including hash keys and
late-attached Apply demand masks. Pure expansion projections/filters preserve
the streaming property. Physical cursors, explicit materialization, recursive
state, volatile programs, and unclassified blocking operators retain their
existing replay owner. Thus a derived expansion may restart from its pinned
values, but an exhausted native storage cursor may never be reopened as a
shortcut to replay.

Apply passes consumer demand to its right iterator. Residual filtering also
preserves demand when its input is restartable expansion, without reducing
physical-storage prefetch to one-row I/O. Demand remains advisory: rejected
rows keep pulling until a match, exhaustion or a real quota/error boundary.
Tests prove that division by zero beyond a delivered LIMIT prefix is deferred,
but occurs when that row is requested. Classification tests explicitly retain
captured ownership for physical reads and volatile AI programs. No executor
limits were raised or input validation skipped. The wider audit below returns
four stale parser-negative dispositions to unresolved; current accounting is
505 implemented / 132 rejected / 113 superseded / 836 unresolved.

The generic long-term follow-up is resumable, bounded prefix replay for
captured/volatile producers, with independently owned readers, spill admission
and fault coverage. This checkpoint preserves those owners; it does not replace
them with unsafe rescanning or claim that every enclosing plan is prefix-lazy.

The full SQL gate also exposed stale compile-only rejection evidence for
`sql-0834`, `sql-0835`, `sql-0879` and `sql-0880`: UNNEST grammar now admits
these complete statements. Those four entries return to unresolved, not
implemented or superseded, until their actual document/index producer contract
is qualified. The immutable source inventory and source rejection expectations
remain unchanged. A dedicated grammar-only test records admission without
granting parity credit. The rejection harness now releases unexpectedly
successful compiled owners and still fails its gate, rather than leaking them
while reporting only the first stale expectation.

### Document SQL-view integration: catalog boundary still required

The current catalog has no persisted view resource. The mega branch discovers
mapped view names by scanning a full table snapshot and reading mappings from
index JSON. That resolver must not be ported as the production architecture.
The desired shape is an indexed, namespace-owned view definition, resolved in
the same catalog epoch as stable source identities, schema layouts and any
index-generation proofs. Its definition and source bindings belong in the
durable catalog, not an implicit index side channel or a global table scan.

SQL binding should expand the pinned view as an authorized derived relation,
retaining dependency identities, RLS/security mode, projected paths and typed
output descriptors. PostgreSQL view-owner versus security-invoker access needs
an explicit owner contract; it must not be approximated by a mutable adapter's last table or
by granting the caller arbitrary physical-source access. Rename/drop/recreate
and source-layout changes must fence stale bindings before opening data cursors.
Public resource/type additions should come from OpenAPI and shared catalog
machinery when that owner contract is implemented. View access and RLS follow
the [PostgreSQL CREATE VIEW rules](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-createview.html),
not the superficially similar SECURITY DEFINER function model.

Document JSON arrays remain JSON on ordinary table reads. A mapped SQL-array
output needs an explicit schema-bound conversion and item type, never inference
from sampled payloads. Index-backed originals need real native candidate/proof
paths plus residual evaluation against the captured cut; ordinary relational
scans over a similarly named fixture are not their evidence. These catalog,
authorization, conversion and producer paths remain unfinished.

### Private SQL-view definition preparation

`sql/view_definition.zig` now prepares owned read-only definitions through the
existing compiler and semantic binder. Its resolver has only authorized point
metadata lookup and cancellation capabilities, not data readers or mutation
callbacks. Repeated lexical references resolve once. Distinct qualifications
retain their SQL identities, while references to one physical table must agree
on logical identity, schema version and digest within one catalog revision.

The retained artifact contains SQL text, stable owner identity, security mode,
ordered output names and exact builtin/array/NUMERIC descriptors, and sorted
source identities with publication guards. Parameters, writable statements,
duplicate output names and inconsistent metadata fail before activation.
Source count, query size, syntax complexity and combined temporary/retained
allocation capacity are bounded. Compiler/binder scratch is released before
returning the artifact; it is not retained with saved definitions. Cancellation
and allocator failures release both regions before ownership transfer.

### Stored-view dependency admission foundation (not activation)

Tracked SQL sources now have a durable, bounded column-identity registry.
Stable IDs survive trusted renames and reordering; dropped/recreated names
receive new IDs through a persisted high-water counter. Exact builtin, array
element and NUMERIC domain signatures distinguish incompatible type changes
without treating DEFAULT, nullability or unrelated-column changes as new
identities. Schema and identity changes share the existing metadata transaction,
standalone publication and committed-Raft apply machinery. Snapshot import and
cold checkpoint validation join identities to the actual source schema and
reject corruption rather than silently repairing it. Ordinary tables do not
create registry state merely because a reader resolves their schema.

View preparation now uses definition-mode relational binding to capture source
column references before constant folding and projection pruning. Stars capture
their creation-time shape; COUNT(*) retains table dependency without depending
on every column. Referenced and unused CTE projections retain their semantic
dependencies. This collection is disabled for ordinary executable binding.
Prepared names/signatures still require transactional resolution to durable
attribute IDs during view publication; they are not execution credentials.

The PostgreSQL oracle in scripts/test_sql_view_catalog.py verifies dependency
behavior and the distinction between owner authorization and session identity.
The owner selects underlying permission checks and RLS policy selection by
default; SQL current_user still evaluates as the caller, including inside the
selected RLS policy. SECURITY INVOKER uses caller authorization. Live owner and
caller grants must be checked at execution, not captured as permanent grants.
Globally impersonating the view owner would implement the wrong semantics.

### SQL view-DDL ingress (publication still guarded)

CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW, output aliases, explicit security_invoker /
security_barrier booleans, ALTER VIEW [IF EXISTS] RENAME, and DROP VIEW
[IF EXISTS] with CASCADE/RESTRICT now lower to compiler-owned view intents in
the existing catalog-DDL interface. Describe performs no mutation. Execution
forwards one intent; it never emulates a view as a physical table. The public
SQL transport remains unchanged; these AST fields are not new public JSON enums.

Preparation reuses the compiled SELECT tree rather than parsing the body a
second time, and retains owned query text, exact outputs, semantic source
dependencies and security mode after compiler teardown. PostgreSQL 18.6 confirms
the lifecycle grammar: CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS is invalid (42601), while
duplicate security options are invalid parameters (22023), not syntax errors.
Compiler limits and allocator-failure cleanup apply to the ingress path.
Source dependencies also retain creation-time ordinal and hiddenness so a
captured star can be reconstructed without admitting later source columns or
silently adopting their new ordering.

Production view execution remains explicitly nonadmitted until namespace-owned
publication, dependency-aware source mutation and fresh owner/RLS delegation
are connected. The next integration must resolve views as tagged relations,
not fabricated ResolvedTable records, and preserve caller SQL expression
identity separately from the subject used for source permission/policy checks.
No original cases receive credit for parsing or a backend probe alone.

PostgreSQL creation admission checks source-schema USAGE, not source-table
SELECT. A view can be created without SELECT and fail when queried until the
owner receives that grant. After creation, revoking source-schema USAGE does
not prevent reads through the stored view if source SELECT still permits them.
Therefore ingress must not reuse the ordinary read-authorizing table resolver,
and execution must bind stored source IDs without repeating source-schema
name-lookup authorization. The PostgreSQL oracle covers both boundaries.

### Native stored-view catalog transaction and recovery boundary

Views now have a namespace-owned catalog resource kind and indexed names, not
an index-JSON mapping or a fabricated physical table. The generic mutation path
rejects opaque view payloads; publication uses a typed private transaction
primitive. Tables and views cannot claim the same namespace name, table/index
claim publication checks view occupancy, and nonempty view namespaces/databases
cannot be retired through the generic catalog planner.

The durable record binds source attribute IDs to the prepared semantic column
references, preserves captured ordering/hiddenness, and owns a monotonic output
attribute registry. Its binding digest covers both the definition and source
IDs. Replacement retains ownership and the existing output-name/type prefix;
appended outputs get new IDs. Omitted security options reset to defaults,
matching PostgreSQL rather than inheriting the old view options.

Publication checks the stored-view SQL cohort floor (55), a verified
occupancy-capable physical namespace root, target identity/generation and source
epochs before writing. Source-attribute bootstrap, the view resource/name
index, catalog counters and authoritative reverse dependency edges commit in
one metadata transaction. A view-only mutation does not invalidate the physical
table/index reconciliation root or trigger an unrelated full catalog rebuild.

Reverse edges include relation existence (column zero, including COUNT(*)) and
each referenced attribute. Source schema changes probe only changed/dropped
attribute IDs; unrelated additions remain compatible. Source retirement checks
dependencies before removing the attribute registry. Stored-state corruption is
not repaired by a successor mutation. Runtime/recovery checks use stable IDs
and exact domains, not a permanent fence on the creation-time schema hash.

View records and reverse edges use the shared catalog snapshot machinery.
Verification checks canonical records, keyed identity, namespace uniqueness,
the activation/namespace root, source attributes and exact forward/reverse edge
coverage. Missing and orphan edges fail installation. Cold checkpoint
verification checks the same invariants, with one source-validation arena at a
time; snapshot cancellation is checked between sources and dependency edges.

This is **not public or distributed SQL-view activation**. The tested primitive
is an owned native catalog transaction, not yet a serialized view Raft command
or an ingress receipt. Command admission/replay, public lifecycle operations,
tagged relation resolution/expansion and fresh owner/RLS delegation remain to
be connected. Ingress still rejects execution before reaching generic table
mutation. No original SQL cases receive credit for this component.

### Stored-view lifecycle and execution-authority integration checkpoint

The private catalog command now carries a typed view lifecycle intent through
the existing apply_system_catalog envelope. Read-only preflight and committed
apply share admission logic; catalog revision/command-hash receipts distinguish
an admitted result from an ambiguous response. Standalone uses the same command
under its existing mutation barrier and standby outbox. CREATE/REPLACE, rename,
RESTRICT and bounded atomic CASCADE operate on namespace-owned resources and
durable IDs. CASCADE plans the entire closure before writing, verifies both
directions of every traversed dependency, and rejects corrupt edges rather
than repairing them. Its explicit limits are 256 views, 16384 dependency edges,
and 3 MiB of retained definition bytes. Cyclic view replacement is admitted,
matching PostgreSQL; expansion reports 42P17 and CASCADE remains finite.

Qualified SQL source reads now return tagged table/view results, including
current attribute registries when requested. Names and IDs are resolved in one
catalog cut; older responses without the tagged-resolution capability cannot
prove a missing view. View mutations include source-attribute changes in the
existing metadata snapshot projection mask. No additional restore system is
introduced.

The relational binder has a request-owned view resolver boundary. Expansion
uses the existing derived-query operators, preserves captured output exposure,
isolates caller CTE/correlation scopes, bounds recursion, and retains the
enclosing invocation, clock, regex budget and SQL settings. Binding-cache keys
include the private resolver scope. Security-barrier nodes stop caller predicate
and dynamic join-filter lineage without preventing optimization of the view's
own producer predicates.

Read authority is separate from the adapter's original caller identity. Policy
proof cache keys include the source schema/catalog epoch and private authority,
not just table ID. Scoped scan, lake rejection and staged-overlay paths reuse
Antfly's existing row-policy proofs and row-filter machinery. Legacy caller and
owner filters are conjunctive and resolve their auth placeholders against their
respective identities. Delegated read tokens select owner policies/roles while
retaining caller expression/settings identity; they cannot authorize writes.
The user manager rechecks caller credentials, owner/caller incarnations and
intermediate view grants under its role-capture lock. CURRENT_USER is a stable
native expression distinct from an API-key-scoped durable settings/session
principal, and installed owner-side policy evaluation preserves that identity.
Invoker views restore the original caller, including the credential's narrower
base-table grants. Installed policy compilation and read capture share the
native schema-to-SQL domain mapping, including NUMERIC and typed arrays.

Quorum admission uses an explicit topology/read-index callback rather than an
unauthenticated primary-key lookup. Admission cannot read rows or bypass RLS;
the subsequently opened cursor still requires its signed row-policy authority.
Only explicitly unpublished read-unavailable responses retry whole-cohort
capture, with bounded backoff and complete cleanup. Individual pages and
ambiguous cursor operations are never replayed.

The public SQL producer now prepares definitions through a definition-only
source-schema loader and submits the typed catalog intent. It derives durable
owners from authenticated user incarnations, never from client definition JSON.
The read adapter resolves stored bodies through ID-bound sources and immutable
request-owned authority contexts. Prepared manifests distinguish tables from
views and fence generation/definition changes. Both the old and new logical
resources require current admin authority for rename. View-resource row filters
run after the complete view projection and before outer predicates, LIMIT and
aggregation, using the existing compiled filter grammar. Their reusable bounded
scratch region does not retain rejected rows.

Production metadata, remote-data and durable-standalone providers advertise the
resolver capability; incomplete/non-durable providers remain closed. The mounted
HTTP/Raft campaign now qualifies the original eight view DDL statements, name
reuse, dependent reads, owner/invoker RLS, legacy caller/owner filter
intersection, native NUMERIC/array policies and owner restart. Pgwire uses the
same producer and read authority: qualification covers protocol execution,
prepared rename/name reuse, definition replacement, and live/detached cursor
revocation, output-filter changes and drop/recreate generation fences.

The document campaign creates an actual document table through the public API
and persists a SQL support_view using jsonb_to_record. Its 38 unchanged original
queries compare PostgreSQL-derived column identities, typed arrays, complete
rows, ordering and SQL NULL flags before and after owner restart. The measured
Debug query cohorts took 939 ms and 1076 ms respectively; this is not a
production throughput or genuinely cold object-store benchmark.

Materialization identity includes the defining authority and outer frame, not
just the immutable AST pointer. Repeated expansions of a stored view cannot
reuse another expansion's correlated producer. jsonb_to_record uses existing
complete-row materialization to convert every declared field once, including
fields discarded by COUNT(*) or outer projections. Strict PostgreSQL errors,
early close and exhaustive allocation-failure cleanup have native regressions.
Schema epoch zero is admitted consistently in policy metadata, installation,
capture and durable table-catalog decoding; it is a valid initial schema, not
missing state.

All 17 API authority/admission contracts and 20 native catalog contracts pass.
The catalog fault campaign delivers committed commands to three independent

### Captured Apply prefix replay

Invariant captured inputs under Apply now retain one suspended iterator instead
of draining it before opening the first reader. A reader at the frontier pulls
one new row, appends an owned replay image and advances. Other readers consume
that image without reopening physical storage or repeating producer effects.
EOF closes the producer once; a producer error is sticky at its frontier.
Abandonment closes suspended iterators before destroying their cached inputs.
Only the Apply iterator that installed an active outer row can retire its
correlation scope; cached consumers cannot destroy a producer's live readers.

The replay owner retains a reusable producer scratch arena. Growing memory
replay can promote to one typed sequential spill run while readers remain live.
Readers own delivered prefix rows across another reader's advancement and
promotion. Pending writer rows are read without flushing one physical record
per pull; readers catch up through subsequently flushed blocks in linear order,
without a per-row offset directory. Sealed replays retain their borrowed-row
fast path. Prefix append/read is explicitly serialized, not a concurrent-file
interface. Spill corruption, quota, cancellation and allocation checks remain
fail-closed; storage failures never authorize producer restart or RAM fallback.

Projection demand is separated from physical page admission: one-row evaluation
does not turn captured scans into one-row I/O. A 4096-row test source delivers a
LIMIT 1 prefix after one physical page without evaluating a later division by
zero, but LIMIT 2 reports that error. Its single-parent PostgreSQL witness avoids
unordered join-orientation ambiguity. A separate multi-parent test verifies one
captured iterator and replayed rows, with exhaustive allocation-failure cleanup.
Independent readers also cross pending-tail flushes and memory/spill promotion.

This activates prefix replay for the invariant Apply cache. Explicit
materialization and recursion-specific caches still use their existing eager
owners; migrating those requires their own lifecycle and fault qualification.
Persisted views remain gated on durable attribute identities, dependency
admission and current owner/RLS delegation. No original case dispositions change.

### Shared materialization and resumable recursive frontiers

Relation-runtime statement/scoped materialized replay owners now use the same
prefix producer as invariant Apply inputs. The eager `staticRows` drain is
removed. Correlated producers are pinned to their highest referenced outer
epoch; scope retirement stops every producer before freeing replay records or
outer values. Nested materializations retain independent readers over the same
captured source, not repeated physical scans.

The first scoped regression exposed another blocking shape: the binder attaches
one known outer row through keyless CROSS JOIN nodes. A proven outer-reference
singleton now streams typed concatenation instead of building a hash table over
the physical side. This optimization requires a keyless, condition-free inner
or CROSS join with an actual outer-reference node. Outer joins, membership,
predicated joins and estimated cardinalities do not receive that shortcut.
The two-epoch regression admits only two relation rows and one physical page
over a 4096-row source, and checks fresh correlated values and allocation faults.

Recursive worklists now retain their seed/step iterator and resume at the
requested output frontier. Each recursive step sees a frozen complete delta;
newly emitted rows cannot feed that same step. UNION duplicate elimination and
UNION ALL multiplicities retain their existing semantics. Multiple consumers
share accumulated owned results without restarting seed or step evaluation.
LIMIT can abandon an otherwise unbounded recursive read; blocking sorts and
complete mutation-source consumers still request the required full input.
Suspended iterators are closed before cached readers, worklists and outer
epochs are retired. Failures are sticky and all current row/work/memory limits
remain in force. Worklist/visited rows still use admitted resident storage;
externalizing that storage and broader recursive coercion/grammar qualification
remain separate work, not claimed here.

Strict output-type assertions found a shared binder bug: VALUES/set inference
discarded concrete integer literal identities and widened int4 to int8. It now
uses the existing scalar literal resolver, keeping NULL/string unknown-type
selection separate. Narrow, wide, smallint and mixed integer cases have native
and PostgreSQL descriptor checks; correlated recursive seed widths are checked
too. No original case dispositions change.

The repeatable owned PostgreSQL gate is
`python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_sql_replay_prefix.py -v`
(with the scripts environment and psycopg installed). Its supplemental cases
check complete values, labels and OIDs for literal/set widths, materialized
prefixes, correlated epoch changes, recursive prefixes, DISTINCT cycles,
blocking finite ordering and combined materialized/recursive scope retirement,
plus deferred division-by-zero SQLSTATE 22012. These controlled heap/VALUES
witnesses are not an ordering guarantee for arbitrary unordered SQL plans.

### Recursive seed-type admission and shared prepared coercion

Recursive binding now selects the term's common builtin/array-element type and
NUMERIC modifier against the already fixed nonrecursive descriptor. A change
to that descriptor fails during metadata binding with SQLSTATE 42804 and a hint
to cast the nonrecursive term to the intended final type. Recursive inference
constraints retain that diagnostic context; unrelated parameter/value errors
keep their existing classification.

Legal narrower terms and unknown string literals use the existing owned
prepared-projection cast pipeline. They are not repaired after rows arrive.
Prepared projection casts also account for modifier differences, not only the
coarse kind and builtin identity. Invalid unknown integer input is 22P02 at
binding; an otherwise correctly typed int4 arithmetic overflow is still 22003
only when that row is requested. A native physical-table regression verifies
that a conflicting term fails with no statement capture, page read or mutation,
even with an empty source and a false recursive predicate.

The synthetic recursive graph fixture now explicitly declares int4 edge
columns, matching its int4 seed and the PostgreSQL oracle's actual DDL. The old
storage-default int8 declaration would require an explicitly int8 seed under
PostgreSQL; accepting that widening was not a valid graph-performance contract.
The source SQL and original inventory are not rewritten or reclassified.

The checked-in replay oracle also verifies recursive type admission via EXPLAIN,
legal implicit term casts, invalid input, runtime overflow and both graph join
orientations. Broader recursive grammar and coercion qualification remain open;
this checkpoint does not assert complete recursive SQL compatibility.

### Exact integer averages and public builtin descriptors

Integer AVG now binds to NUMERIC for int2/int4/int8 inputs. Grouped vectors,
DISTINCT reducers, spill/checkpoint replay and associative partial merges retain
one i128 sum and one count, rather than a floating mean or one allocated NUMERIC
per input. Finalization divides exact allocation-free integer views using the
bounded native NUMERIC kernel, preserving PostgreSQL's output scale and owning
the result in the consumer region. Invalid floating-state checkpoints and sums
outside their declared integer-width/count bounds reject before import.

Ordinary running and sliding integer AVG frames use the existing removable
constant-width state; they no longer need the indexed aggregate tree. Excluded
frames still combine exact indexed sums/counts before the same finalization.
This is a state-shape improvement, not a measured throughput claim. Exhaustive
final-output allocation failures, widened partial sums, consumer ownership,
forced 1000-group spilling and DISTINCT reductions have Debug coverage.

The window qualification also found two builtin-descriptor issues. NTILE's
result is int4, not int8; ranking functions retain int8 through symbolic set
inference. NTILE accepts int2/int4 arguments and NULL, rejects int8 overloads
before statement acquisition, and reports PostgreSQL 22014 for nonpositive
bucket counts. HTTP description serialization now retains every supplied
scalar builtin identity, not only NUMERIC and arrays; internal NULL provenance
still never escapes. The existing public schema already permits these widths,
so no new wire enum or generated API type is introduced.

The separate numeric-window campaign keeps sql-1366 and sql-1376 unchanged.
Its int4 amount and int8 quantity domains have 24 nonempty native rows, unique

### Captured ranked frontiers and demand-driven SQL projection

The shared native search cursor now owns the ranked frontier and, for relational
tables, the primary reader captured under the same statement fences. Iteration
hydrates only the demanded page, checks captured primary membership even for
ID-only reads, and retains SQL-null provenance separately from JSONB null. Page
layouts, identities and selected values survive cursor closure. Failed page
allocations or later-row failures do not advance the frontier. Cursor closure
releases the primary snapshot, authorization lease and native result exactly
once; no apply fence remains held during user iteration.

Lite/C preparation narrows native stored-field projection to the physical fields
SQL demands and disables unselected highlighting after validating the complete
original request. Relational ranking no longer eagerly hydrates redundant JSON
documents: its native reader projects typed values into the consumer page.
Document ranking still captures projected source packets under the native lease;
the cursor defers packet materialization and selected-cell ownership, not the
underlying document capture. This is not yet a deferred document point-reader.
Table identity, schema version and storage mode are revalidated during capture.
Native page-owned relational payloads avoid a second selected-cell deep copy;
borrowed document/vector payloads still receive owned copies.

Four shared Debug regressions cover prefix demand, alias projection, exact
NUMERIC scale, JSONB/SQL nulls, metadata-only iteration, ownership after close,
atomic failed pages and exhaustive initialization/hydration allocation faults.
The full Debug SQL gate passes 866 core and 234 extracted tests, with four opt-in
skips, zero failures/leaks and 21/21 successful steps in
`/private/tmp/antfly-sql-search-cursor-full-debug.log`. The focused gate including
the opt-in benchmark passes all five tests in
`/private/tmp/antfly-sql-search-cursor-owned-focused-debug.log`.

The benchmark isolates hydration over a preallocated 10,000-hit frontier with
512-byte selected text and two logical aliases. For demands of 1, 128 and 10,000
rows, primary lookups are respectively 1, 128 and 10,000; peak owned bytes are
6,844, 310,728 and 38,091,222. Ranking, I/O and frontier allocation are excluded:
these measurements establish prefix-proportional hydration, not an end-to-end
query speedup. The checked-in PostgreSQL projection oracle additionally verifies
SQL NULL versus JSONB null and exact JSONB numeric display scale, including the
retained `.0` in `9007199254740993.0`; it does not qualify search/ranking cases.

### Real-owner default DDL and publication acknowledgement

The next catalog cohort uses unchanged sql-0741, sql-0742 and sql-0743 through
the existing mounted metadata/data-owner fixture. It owns CREATE, original
ALTER statements, omitted/explicit NULL/DEFAULT inserts, complete postimages,
the serving schema observation and a cold data-owner restart. Existing primary
bytes and write versions must remain unchanged across default alterations;
future inserts and UPDATE DEFAULT must use the newly committed declarations.
Unknown-column rejection must preserve both schema version and table rows.
The independent PostgreSQL oracle is `scripts/test_sql_default_lifecycle.py`,
available through `make sql-default-lifecycle-oracle-check`.

The real-owner run exposed a production acknowledgement race, not a missing
scalar default evaluator: migration finalization could clear the predecessor
read layout after a successful schema CAS but before its acknowledgement read.
Exact transient-descriptor comparison then reported an unknown mutation outcome.
The reproducer is `/private/tmp/antfly-sql-default-lifecycle-read-cut-debug.log`;
the fixture does not replay that DDL or reinterpret the error as success.

Acknowledgement now reuses the finalizer's deterministic transformation. It
accepts the exact replacement or that exact finalized successor, preserving
the original ordered stamp. Owner, active schema and read-layout mismatches
reject before candidate allocation; all remaining descriptor fields compare
exactly after transformation. Arbitrary later DDL, named-index changes and
other supersessions remain unknown. This is narrowly scoped logical-publication
evidence, not a durable per-command outcome journal or a solution for a wholly
lost public response. It introduces neither replay nor an unbounded receipt log.

The Debug gate `antfly-api-sql-default-lifecycle-test` selects the real-owner
campaign plus strict successor/rejection, ordered-stamp and exhaustive
allocation-failure regressions. Pure reads and definitely unadmitted write
preparation may repeat only the specific statement-read rejection within one
15-second deadline. SQLSTATE 53300 alone is insufficient: it also represents
post-commit visibility waits. The fixture requires the exact read-admission
diagnostic, explicit retry permission, idle state and absence of every mutation,
admission or transaction receipt. DDL, admitted writes, malformed diagnostics
and other failures never receive that retry. Regression gates include the
production mutation-receipt classifier and the fixture's stricter predicate.
The initial sandbox run failed at loopback bind before running the campaign;
the mounted validation requires local socket access.

### Bounded publication progress and original CREATE qualification

The publication timeout is now fixed at the shared metadata proof boundary.
Source and candidate verification retain bounded progress across completely
observed heartbeat/report commits. A private replica-local input-domain fence
tracks committed watermarks under the apply lane; its closed typed whitelist
contains only store heartbeat and report updates/baselines. Every other command,
observation gap or implicit catalog-index rebuild invalidates reuse. Unknown
standalone/import/repair mutations and namespace installation bracket commits
with O(1) namespace invalidation. Opening a read also fences namespace races,
including foreign mutations that leave the Raft watermark unchanged.

This is a scheduling hint, not publication authority. Completed evidence is
explicitly rebound to an observed exact applied cut only within the same input
domain and with exact source/job/root checks. Publication retains its strict
transactional applied-position and capability checks. There are no new durable
keys, extra LSM writes, public ABI fields or production reporter activation.
The pending reporter namespace-generation activation remains unenabled.

### Expression-index qualification and remaining owner/access architecture

The next original cohort contains sql-0017, sql-0712 through sql-0718, and
sql-0722/sql-0723. The independent PostgreSQL 18.6 oracle
`scripts/test_sql_expression_index_lifecycle.py` passes all ten subcases,
including complete mutation postimages, normalized UNIQUE collisions, inactive
partial-index rows, predicate transitions and delete/reinsert behavior.
PostgreSQL rejects concat/concat_ws index keys with 42P17 because those functions
are stable, even with text arguments. They must not be silently accepted as
immutable text-only overloads. Native immutable-expression lowering already
preserves that distinction.

The mounted positive gate
`antfly-api-sql-expression-index-lifecycle-test` remains deliberately strict:
it requires real owner builds, preserved generations across cold restart,
complete postimages and EXPLAIN-selected index reads after mutations. Its first
run failed before sql-0017 admission. The distributed fixture has no standalone
native-owner binding, and metadata correctly rejects borrowing native ordered
authority for a Raft owner. That semantic rejection was absent from the compiled
failure registry, producing repeated undeclared-error warnings and finally a
deadline diagnostic. The failure is retained in
`/private/tmp/antfly-sql-expression-index-original-debug.log`.

UnsupportedNativeIndexOwner now has an append-only runtime status (802) and
shared failure ABI version 65. It round-trips without becoming generic internal
failure. The mounted nonadmission regression independently requires 0A000,
nonretryable completion, unchanged schema/owner and no durable index-publication
head, then verifies the table remains writable after owner restart. This is a
diagnostic/authority fix, not qualification of the positive original. No
standalone reporter registration, generation switching or retirement is enabled.

Two shared architectural requirements remain before this cohort is complete:

1. **Raft-owned index lifecycle.** Mount the existing lifecycle phases on
   data-Raft commands with exact owner/namespace/schema/term guards and durable
   idempotent receipts at committed term/index positions. Preparation, bounded
   source pages and artifact transfer stay outside serialized apply; local
   progress, UNIQUE claims, installation and writer fencing commit atomically
   through the authoritative group. Metadata must select the actual supported
   authority and dispatch through an explicit authority adapter, never label
   Raft execution native. Publication requires complete current-owner coverage;
   cancellation and recovery must retain authentic positions and provenance.
   Decoder/support admission must be in place before activation. The independent
   native reporter-namespace activation restriction remains unchanged.
2. **Shared expression/partial read access plans.** The schema cache currently
   exposes only direct, nonpartial tuple keys to SQL access planning. Retain
   immutable typed expression/comparison identities and compiled partial
   predicates in the schema layout; match bound SQL programs in that same
   domain. Prepare row-independent typed probe operands once per statement,
   retaining the full residual filter. Reuse the native bounded implication
   machinery rather than inventing SQL-only predicate equivalence. Carry an
   explicit schema/generation-bound index span through coordinated snapshot and
   range-proof capture, and use the same access plan for EXPLAIN and execution.
   Simple scans and relation-graph scans must share that planner. An unproven
   implication or incompatible comparison domain must not narrow a scan.

NOT VALID/VALIDATE is a separate catalog gap: declared validity must remain
distinct from future-write enforcement and disposable local scan coverage.
Ordinary validated additions need an atomic publication barrier; NOT VALID
must preserve existing rows and enforce future writes without pretending a
background scan makes the declaration validated. Explicit validation needs a
named, owner-fenced cohort and durable completion before catalog validity flips.

### Bound key language and immutable operator preparation

Index-key lowering can now consume a selected instruction of an already-bound
scalar program. It preserves the authoritative implicit casts and builtin
domains instead of rebinding source SQL under a different expected type.
Canonical names come from the caller's verified ordinal/type layout; this
helper does not grant alias, table or schema authority. Topological instruction
suffixes beyond the selected root are excluded from key-preparation budgets.
Unrelated stable calls, parameters and deferred arithmetic errors are not
demanded. Reachable parameters or mutable operations cannot become stored keys.

Shared schema-expression preparation also constructs immutable operator
parents directly over arena-owned children, copying only argument vectors and
owned headers. It no longer serializes and reparses those complete child trees
for each ordinary operator. Literal packets retain their owning conversion
because they can borrow a program or temporary constant-folding region.
Argument nodes are immutable after publication into a parent; wire serialization
still emits the same tree. No schema/storage format or capability activation
changes. The ownership regression closes the borrowed program before checking
the retained JSONB literal and its exact `1.2300e2` token; physical
canonicalization and JSONB display formatting are not conflated with ownership.

The full Debug gate passes 1,108 tests with four existing opt-in skips, zero
failures/leaks and 21/21 build steps in
`/private/tmp/antfly-sql-bound-index-key-operator-full-debug.log`. It covers
qualified names, bounds/type mismatches, comparison-domain casts, deferred

### Request-owned complete index declarations and iterator failure integrity

SQL table bindings now retain immutable ordered-index declarations separately
from the existing direct-total probe list. The descriptors preserve mixed
column/expression key order, declared expression result domains, collation,
direction, NULL placement, included columns and every partial predicate,
including constant-false membership and exact numeric operand tokens.
They describe eligibility only: no readiness, owner coverage, publication
pointer, authorization decision or predicate proof is cached.

The server schema cache derives these descriptors on a miss and clones the
compact owned trees directly on hits, without stringify/reparse. Both cached
and uncached paths survive parser retirement and cache eviction. Cache retention
remains bounded by the existing entry budget; oversized entries use the
statement-owned fallback. Existing direct-total consumers cannot accidentally
use an expression/partial declaration. Malformed native key combinations,
predicate shapes, unsupported access channels and declaration limits fail closed.
The regression covers SQL-lowered definitions, mixed composite keys, exact
integers above binary64 precision, constant-false membership, fallback,
eviction and exhaustive allocation failures.

The first broad Debug run exposed a swallowed allocation failure in UNNEST's
exhaustion pull. The focused reproduction and captured failure stack identify
`ArenaAllocator.reset(retain_with_limit)` consolidation, not array expansion,
at the induced allocation cut. Retention can allocate even when no later row
needs allocating. UNNEST now clears borrowed cells before resetting and
propagates failure. Analogous recursive, scalar-Apply, membership and hash/spill
join iterator retention paths also propagate failure. Scratch retention and
normal reuse remain enabled; this is not a free-all workaround. The existing
UNNEST allocation-fault and capture-close contract passes unchanged; temporary
diagnostic instrumentation was removed.

### Typed native-key matching and lossless NUMERIC ingress

Both server and Lite/C resolvers now derive complete index declarations through
the same schema vocabulary. Each declared key is prepared with the native
expression compiler's semantic fingerprint, result kind and precise builtin
identity. Server cache hits copy these fixed-width identities along with owned
trees; they do not rebind declarations. Query preparation can lower a selected
already-bound instruction into the same native key language once and reuse its
identity for candidate comparisons. Equality matching preserves NUMERIC
modifiers, implicit casts and collation domains: binary/C/POSIX agree, while
case-insensitive versus binary comparisons do not silently match. Unprepared
keys fail closed. Direction and NULL placement remain separate tuple properties.

The compiler-only typed table view borrows names from the authorized pinned
table and owns its column vector in the preparation region. It is not a storage
schema, native capability grant, readiness record, partial-membership proof or
snapshot/range proof. Qualification/ordinal authority belongs to the bound scan;
the matcher does not strip arbitrary aliases. Cached declarations are checked
against this typed view after eviction and on uncached fallback, including
exhaustive allocation cuts. Native key identity preparation also unwinds every
allocation failure without retaining the borrowed source table or VM arena.

The real C ABI regression exposed two existing ingress gaps: its resolver
rejected native NUMERIC columns and dropped NUMERIC modifiers, and plain numeric
assignments used coarse JSON coercion before typed storage admission. The
resolver now preserves those domains. Plain NUMERIC literals, SQL NULL and
unknown string inputs enter the shared scalar preparation pipeline. Constant
UPDATE values are evaluated/owned once per statement, not per target row.
The prepared literal test repeatedly evaluates cached exact values with a
zero-byte scratch allocator; this is a component allocation result, not an
end-to-end query latency claim.

An assignment-context regression then demonstrated why outer expectations must
not substitute an operator overload: ABS(bigint_min) must overflow before a
NUMERIC target receives its result. Integral expressions retain their original
kernel and use an explicit conversion instruction at the contextual boundary.
This also preserves typed quantified/set producers and SQL NULL propagation;
the unchanged nullable quantified-query regression passes alongside the
assignment overflow contract. Explicitly typed text remains an assignment error.

The C ABI request parser now preserves JSON numeric tokens until contextual
parameter preparation rather than first rounding decimal input through f64.
The real database test covers values above binary64 precision, declared scale,
composite expression/partial indexes with included columns, binding ownership
after database retirement, exact UPDATE postimages, rejected-assignment
postimages, and an unquoted high-precision JSON parameter across another cold
restart. Temporary diagnostic tracing has been removed.

PostgreSQL 18.6 (180006) independently verifies these literal, parameter,
overflow, assignment and quantified expectations as well as the ten original
expression-index lifecycle subcases. This oracle is not native owner-recovery
or indexed-read qualification. Validation logs are retained under
`/private/tmp/antfly-sql-index-numeric-parameter-postgres-final.log` and the
`antfly-sql-numeric-explicit-boundary-*` / `antfly-sql-native-index-*` /
`antfly-sql-embedded-index-*` Debug logs; final gate totals are recorded below.

selection and partial implication, invocation-owned probes, fresh generation and

EXPLAIN plan. Lite also needs bounded immutable-layout reuse per database owner
instead of deriving the view for each resolve. Raft-backed index publication and
per-constraint NOT VALID/VALIDATE intent remain incomplete. No original
dispositions change: 531 implemented / 810 unresolved.

### Shared bound expression equality access

Materialized and streaming single-table SQL reads now share preparation of
expression-equality hints over their already-authorized scalar programs. Native
key identities are matched without rebinding declarations or source SQL. Only
row-independent immutable probe operands are evaluated; unrelated predicate
errors, stable/volatile calls, disjunctions and mismatched typed domains do not
become eager query work. Unknown text literals acquire their comparison domain
losslessly, while explicitly different domains are not narrowed to manufacture
an index point. Exact integral-to-NUMERIC conversion remains lossless.

Probe preparation owns a bounded temporary region per needed key, polls the
statement cancellation owner and copies only admitted typed operands into the
request region. Optional preparation-limit exhaustion falls back to the normal
access path; actual backing allocation failures and cancellation propagate.
Exhaustive allocation cuts cover the new preparation owner. No-index tables
return before allocating this preparation state.
Temporary caps also reserve enclosing request headroom. A 256-byte parent-budget
regression proves optional preparation can decline the hint without marking the
parent exhausted or retaining allocations. Fault enumeration forces growing
arenas through allocate/copy paths rather than depending on the debug heap's
address-dependent in-place resize availability.

The server and embedded adapters transport these advisory hints to the existing
native snapshot-local planner. Expression keys can extend a mixed direct/key
equality prefix, preserving independent direction and NULL ordering. Existing
READY checks, schema/head fences, partial membership implication, bounded
candidate/cardinality work and covering checks still select the actual access
path. SQL retains the complete predicate and does not push LIMIT through an
incomplete residual. An unavailable expression key can still leave a useful
leading-column prefix; it must neither force a needless primary scan nor narrow
that prefix using an unproven key.

Read-only access does not enable staged-write overlays accidentally: embedded
active transactions keep their existing guarded path, and server staged writes
disable this hint preparation. Existing coordinated primary-range proofs remain
conservative for automatic access; this work does not claim precise indexed
phantom protection or a new capability/readiness proof.

Remaining activation includes relation/join lineage-aware preparation before
snapshot capture, additional range/temporal probe domains, one EXPLAIN/execution
access plan, bounded embedded immutable-layout reuse, and genuine Raft-backed
index publication authority. Per-constraint NOT VALID/VALIDATE intent is also
unfinished. Original dispositions remain 531 implemented / 810 unresolved.

### Physical-plan exact tuple protection

The native retained reader now records a complete-tuple equality domain from
its selected READY access path. Explicit full-key bounds and automatic mixed
direct/expression equality prefixes share this metadata. Full key arity is
proved separately from physical successor bounds: a composite prefix must not
be mistaken for a point merely because its upper bound is nextPrefix(lower).
Successor comparison needs no additional tuple allocation. All fallible
preparation finishes before schema/index lifetime pins are cloned.

Read-session range protection consumes that physical plan, not ingress syntax.
Eligible automatic full-key reads now capture one existing index-tuple
generation counter on the same retained snapshot rather than 257 primary
bucket counters. This reduces read-set and prepared-guard amplification while
allowing unrelated tuples to change. It adds no new counter format or writer
tracking protocol: inserts, key moves and non-indexed payload updates already
advance or reserve the same canonical tuple identity. Empty point reads guard
future members too. Partial-index membership and generation/READY checks remain
mandatory; prefixes, ranges and unavailable-index fallbacks remain conservative.

The new native regression compares automatic and explicit proof identities,
allows an unrelated update, blocks matching inserts/key moves/payload updates,
detects stale observations, permits excluded partial-index rows, protects an
empty lookup against a matching phantom and verifies counters after cold
reopen. A separate allocation-free successor contract covers descending
trailing bytes and non-point bounds. The observed guard-scope reduction is
257 to one for this full-key fixture, not a general query latency claim.

This closes automatic full-tuple proof derivation, not general interval/phantom
protection or distributed index publication. Join access facts still need
lineage- and sharing-aware preparation before cursor capture, and EXPLAIN must
consume the shared physical access plan. Raft-backed index publication and
per-constraint activation remain unfinished. No original cases are newly
qualified: 531 implemented / 810 unresolved.

The pre-existing exact-span counter ledger also needs bounded reclamation for
live-generation churn. This change neither creates a new counter family nor
deletes old observations. Counters must not simply disappear while an older
unprepared read can still be admitted: absent-to-absent reuse would introduce
ABA. The long-term retirement design must fence stale observations and preserve
prepared guard reservations, with bounded work and explicit generation scope.

### Relation-aware access preparation before capture

Relational scans now prepare immutable typed access facts before opening any
statement cursor, including the shared capture used by source-aware mutations
and RETURNING. The binding caches an immutable relation DAG and its immediate
dominators. Execution prepares only parameter-dependent operands, in bounded
scratch memory, and copies owned facts into statement-local scan requests.
Neither the cached graph nor the original bound scans are mutated.

Canonical column lineage supports direct predicates, primary-key equalities
and matching expression equalities through joins and passthrough projections.
Outer-join ON facts apply only to the nonpreserved input; WHERE facts on
null-extended inputs must reject a synthetic NULL row. Shared producers require
domination, so a filter on one materialized CTE consumer cannot narrow the
producer used by another. Intrinsic producer filters still qualify. LIMIT,
OFFSET, cardinality, aggregation, windows, volatile derived projections,
set/recursive coercions and explicit materialization remain optimizer fences.
Every SQL residual remains authoritative and row goals are cleared when facts
are added. Native READY/partial-membership and retained-snapshot checks remain
unchanged. Exhausting optional planner scratch falls back to original scans;
actual allocation failure, cancellation and final publication failure propagate.

Validation exposed a separate NUMERIC inference error: relation shape lowering
inserted a coarse number cast and thereby inferred FLOAT8 before executable
binding. Shape inference and executable binding now share comparison-operand
construction. Unknown NUMERIC inputs preserve their exact domain, explicit
floating descriptors preserve PostgreSQL's mixed-domain behavior, and column
typmods do not round comparison operands. Both lowering passes receive the
invocation's authoritative parameter descriptors. Regressions cover aliased and
unaliased JSON number tokens above 2^53, explicit floating inputs, near misses
and cold native reopen.

This closes statement-local relation access placement, not join equivalence
propagation or arbitrary computed-projection substitution. Unified physical
EXPLAIN/execution planning, broader typed range domains, Raft-owned index
publication, per-constraint activation, immutable embedded layout reuse and
bounded conflict-counter retirement remain unfinished. Original dispositions
remain 531 implemented / 132 rejected / 113 superseded / 810 unresolved.

### Raft owner admission, drain and reservation kernel (not mounted)

Private UNIQUE candidate preparation now has one authority-neutral implementation
shared by native and Raft controls. It validates the actual persisted source
authority; the authority selector is an internal construction parameter, not an
RPC capability. Parsing, schema/layout compilation and owned immutable inputs
remain outside apply exclusion.

The Raft kernel has distinct admission, drained-fence and reservation commands.
The trusted state-machine caller supplies the actual owner group and committed
term/index separately from the command. Each phase effect and its ordered apply
watermark share one store transaction. Three checksummed fixed-size slots retain
the original phase positions, binding the full immutable job and effect.
Retries at later positions advance the watermark without reburning generations
or changing the original receipt. Zero/conflicting positions, backward terms,
foreign groups/namespaces, native authority, stale catalogs and undrained
predecessors fail closed. No native source clock advances or native receipt is
minted.

Receipt recovery and cold owner verification check those cuts against the same
snapshot's applied watermark, schema, catalogs, manifest and topology fence.
Configured standby/mirror publication remains explicitly unsupported by this
new apply entry point until its ordered envelope is implemented; the shared
replication mutation lease follows the existing publisher/snapshot ordering.
Hidden restore-staging owners are rejected and retain their existing scoped
restore command path.

The LSM kernel regression exercises original-cut recovery across leader terms
and cold reopen, duplicate application, pre-admission rejection, predecessor
transaction drain, corruption rejection, configured-mirror nonadmission,
allocation-failure ownership and rollback at every phase/marker write boundary.
These are real storage transaction contracts with supplied committed-entry
identities, NOT a distributed consensus/leadership qualification.

Complete distributed activation still requires:

- Private data-Raft and standby envelope codecs, strict public nonadmission,
  decoder support and an all-member durable capability barrier.
- Authenticated server receiver/proposal dispatch, guarded by the actual
  leader, owner namespace and immutable metadata decision.
- Position-aware bounded source/build pages, streaming claims, target
  provenance and resumable checkpoints using real Raft cuts.
- Inventory validation, schema/catalog installation, publication coverage and
  cancellation/release/GC through the same authority-specific transaction path.
- Metadata's real Raft authority adapter and distributed fault campaigns plus
  successful execution of the original positive index cases.

Metadata's unsupported-Raft guard is unchanged. No standalone reporter namespace
or retirement activation is enabled. Original dispositions remain 531 implemented
/ 132 rejected / 113 superseded / 810 unresolved; these kernel contracts do not
qualify the unfinished distributed DDL cohort.

### Private Raft index control transport and two-store recovery

The admission/drain/reservation kernel now has a data-only private batch
contract, separate from preparation and store apply. The exact wire frame rejects
public requests, unprefixed aliases, row-semantics wrappers, unknown fields,
caller-supplied positions and mixed mutations. Borrowed-tree framing and input
size checks run before typed manifest duplication or row normalization. The
isolated-request validator checks every request field against its default shape;
owned empty arrays are compared by semantic length, not pointer identity.

Committed-entry dispatch supplies the actual group, term and index separately.
The group-aware adapter validates isolation and group identity before replay
checks, skips already-applied entries before preparing against a newer catalog,
and otherwise commits the native effect and ordered marker atomically. Ordinary
local batches, unscoped ordered adapters and the not-yet-implemented standby
envelope cannot silently drop the control.

Raft batch protocol 23 denotes support for these three controls ONLY. The
projection decoder requires a durable protocol barrier, the actual matching
group and a configured native delegate before accepting an entry. It cannot
acknowledge a projection-only no-op as index progress. This is not a complete
distributed-index lifecycle capability: source/build/install/cancel and standby
still require their own complete implementation and versioned admission.
The projection's immutable mount contract is also checked by DataStateMachine:
if the actual delegate is absent, entries and snapshots are rejected before
projection writes or applied-index publication. A configured projection flag
alone cannot stand in for the second store.
Both the direct projection builder and compiled storage consumer preserve this
mount requirement. The compiled client retains the exact construction setting
sent through its ABI, and the managed-host adapter exposes it to the state
machine. Its regression rejects an unmounted client before even accessing the
foreign handle.

The two-store regression uses the real projection store, LSM native owner,
committed batch decoder, group-aware adapter and DataStateMachine applied sink.
It rejects missing/old barriers, missing delegates and foreign groups, and
injects failures between projection commit, native commit and applied-index
publication. Both stores are reopened before replay; phase receipts keep their
original committed cuts across subsequent terms and retries. Allocation probes
also cover owned codec cleanup and rejection without a derived allocation.
These are supplied-entry state-machine fault tests, not network-consensus or
metadata-leadership qualification.

Generic proposal dispatch explicitly rejects these controls before consulting
Raft state or appending a barrier. A decoded binding is NOT metadata permission.
The dedicated independently authorized receiver and complete source/build,
claim/install/cancel/standby lifecycle remain unfinished; metadata PrepareCut's
unsupported-Raft guard remains unchanged. No standalone reporter namespace or
retirement activation is enabled. Original case dispositions remain 531
implemented / 132 rejected / 113 superseded / 810 unresolved.

### Authority-specific metadata binding and coherent Raft owner inspection

Immutable index-owner identity is now a shared data-only contract, not a native
execution capability. Native and Raft metadata conversion use the same immutable
plan/owner/fence/schema/input binding checks, with explicit authority on every
entry point. Native facades retain their existing shape. Raft admission accepts
only a matching admission projection; hot fence/reserve commands need no manifest
and canonicalize only the command copy, never the observed durable job phase.
The manifest constructor is shared without repeating candidate compilation.
Execution also binds the metadata cluster incarnation to the immutable catalog
guard. Historical journal verification uses a pure dispatch/binding verifier
with the actual recorded incarnation, not a fabricated zero-incarnation execution
decision. The verifier separately checks the head/owner/plan linkage; matching
historical provenance remains distinct from current permission. Native producer
fixtures now derive their incarnation from the same guard, and both authority
paths explicitly reject a valid but foreign cluster incarnation.

The Raft owner inspection entry point takes the trusted actual group separately
from the metadata identity. A single read snapshot checks the persisted namespace
and Raft authority, exact job identity, phase receipts, applied watermark, topology
fence, immutable inputs and schema/catalog preimage. It rejects hidden restore
staging, mismatched identities and corrupt cuts; it never creates a receipt or
advances the native clock. Absence is information, not permission or a cancel ACK.

The metadata projection tests exercise both authority paths, admitted manifest
identity, wrong-authority/request/binding rejection and reserved retries. Their
synthetic bindings and supplied logical positions are conversion fixtures, NOT
storage or distributed evidence. The LSM kernel contract separately verifies real
owner inspection before/after admission, fencing and reservation, through cold
reopen and receipt corruption, plus group/namespace/staging/native-alias rejection.

The independently authorized receiver and compiled-owner observation/preparation
bridge remain to be mounted. They must preserve the actual leader term and owner
scope through protocol admission and recheck the decision/binding before proposal.
Full source/build/claim/install/cancel/standby processing still needs real tagged
positions throughout, retained recovery and distributed fault qualification.
Qualification must also cover a busy drain rejection followed by transaction
resolution and retry through the real server delegate, including both store
watermarks and typed proposal outcomes, not only supplied-entry kernel calls.
PrepareCut's unsupported-Raft guard and generic proposal nonadmission are unchanged;
no standalone reporter namespace or retirement activation is enabled. Original

Raft owner's binding, original fence/reservation receipts and apply watermark.
These values come from one read transaction; the trusted opaque handle supplies
the actual group. The observer checks namespace/authority, catalogs, immutable
inputs and durable cuts before returning. It neither selects physical index IDs
nor changes a job, allocates an index, signs progress or supplies metadata permission.
An unprovisioned directory without durable identity fails closed; an empty
relational table with its metadata-authoritative schema is a valid owner.

The response contract requires its version and validates exact identity,
authority, phase/action, catalog digests, original-position evidence and ordering
against the same watermark. The evidence hash is shared with retained-cut storage
without changing its encoding; it detects inconsistent data, but does not
authenticate a caller or prove commit by itself. Native positions cannot substitute for Raft
positions. Schema/catalog lengths are checked before hashing their bounded
private-job preimages.

The ABI admits at most 4 KiB of identity JSON and 32 KiB of response. It rejects
unknown input fields and caller-supplied positions, preserves typed failure
identity and checks cancellation/deadlines before and after read and after
serialization. The typed client validates the failure boundary/operation and the
decoded observation before releasing the response buffer. Native controls and
Raft reads share the bounded JSON response mechanism; allocation is capped before
serialization, and native controls retain their pre-commit response allocation.

Real-store tests cover no-job/admitted/fenced/reserved states, original cuts after
later-term retries, incoherent/native positions, missing cuts, tampered evidence,
caller-position rejection and cancellation at all three checkpoints. A read
transaction pinned before admission still observes the old absence and watermark
after admission commits, while a fresh read observes the new job. Corrupt retained
cuts also reject observation rather than becoming absence or an ACK.
The separately compiled-provider test exercises typed reads on a provisioned empty
table, wrong-table/deadline failures and the unchanged generic proposal guard.
These are storage/ABI contracts, not network consensus or complete SQL qualification.

### Owner-selected Raft admission preparation across the compiled boundary

Read-only admission preparation now accepts the immutable metadata admission
header and raw bounded manifest and returns only a versioned physical binding.
The actual handle supplies table/group scope; the owner checks its durable
namespace and source authority. The shared `PreparedAdmission` owns the single
candidate compilation and is reused by both advisory preparation and committed
command preparation. Only the latter constructs base64 transport bytes. No
physical index ID, committed position, signature or verification flag is accepted
from the coordinator by the preparation ABI.

Preparation is advisory, not a reservation or promise that apply will succeed.
Catalog/schema CAS and the durable metadata/leader/capability checks remain
mandatory at proposal/apply. The bridge does not admit a job, change a watermark,
advance the native clock or open the generic proposal guard. Its response is
bounded to 16 KiB before serialization; admission JSON is bounded to 8 KiB and
the raw manifest to the existing immutable-input limit before dereferencing.
Cancellation/deadline checks bracket compilation and serialization; cancellation
during compilation prevents returning a result but does not yet interrupt each
individual compiler phase. The client validates exact admission identity,
authority, phase and manifest digest and preserves the typed failure envelope.

### Leased Raft owner facts and rejected-entry snapshot qualification

Raft observation/preparation now use the provisioned owner's existing admission
queue and a shared identity-scoped lease helper. The returned root generation is
copied from that exact lease before release, never recovered from a later route
lookup. Both adapters retain deadline/cancellation checks and the compiled
owner's durable authority/namespace validation. Root provenance alone grants no
leadership, enrollment, metadata permission or signing authority. Native controls
retain their existing behavior through the same renamed acquisition helper.

An important receiver invariant is now explicit: `Observation.applied` is the
native store's last committed mutation identity, **not** the host's completed
Raft prefix or ReadIndex. A rejected prepare or protocol barrier may advance the
host without changing that mutation receipt. The native snapshot format records
both `through_index` and `native_index` and explicitly permits the latter to lag.
Advancing a fabricated native receipt merely to equalize those values would be
the wrong fix, as would treating a completed rejected entry as a fence ACK.

not the actual snapshot contract. Qualification now preserves the distinction
and checks typed rejection outcomes between successful entries. The new snapshot

rejected conflicting prepare. It captures both stores at host prefix three with
native mutation two, materializes the snapshot, interrupts restore after raw
projection preparation, retries publication, and verifies the restored mutation
cut and winning intent by rejecting the conflicting prepare again. No protocol
guard or rejection classification is weakened. These use supplied committed
entries and a real compiled owner/LSM, not network consensus qualification.
